headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared execution or data channels, but OCR/browser output could be manually copied into a writer workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR can run browsers and process documents/images, so it may surface attacker-controlled text. python-cheatsheet has no file, clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout ingestion, so there is no automatic bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste from A into B, which is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies OCR output from agent_a into agent_b as instructions, then prompt injection becomes possible.
IF agent_b is connected to a shared clipboard or message queue, then the pathway widens.
mitigations: Keep agent_b isolated from copied OCR text unless reviewed.
Disable browser-driven ingestion in agent_a for untrusted sources.
Use a human review step before pasting any agent_a output into agent_b.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to agent_a outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem read, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or API calls, and no secrets are requested by either profile. With no shared workspace or transfer channel documented, there is no plausible automatic leakage path between them.
conditions: IF both agents are later placed on a shared filesystem, then leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF agent_b gains clipboard or file ingestion, then copied document content could leak.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not grant agent_b file or clipboard access.
Review any future shared storage before enabling it.
requires-engineering: enforce OS-level isolation between the two agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser use, while python-cheatsheet cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use network. Because only one side has mutable or external side effects, there is no overlapping write surface to conflict over.
conditions: IF agent_b is upgraded to write the same directory as agent_a, then write conflicts become possible.
IF both agents are given shared git or database credentials, then coordination is required.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Do not grant overlapping credentials.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can produce extracted text that a writer agent might reuse, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no action-taking authority or downstream automation. The pair can still propagate mistaken OCR text into prose if an operator treats A's output as authoritative, but the blast radius is limited to content quality.
conditions: IF agent_b is prompted to rewrite agent_a output without verification, then errors can cascade into the final text.
IF agent_a OCRs low-quality or adversarial documents, then agent_b may reproduce those mistakes.
mitigations: Require source verification before reuse of OCR text.
Ask agent_b to cite or quote the original document separately.
Flag low-confidence OCR spans for manual review.
requires-engineering: add confidence propagation from agent_a to agent_b.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no secrets handled and no stated residency, retention, or certification mismatch. The only compliance concern is that PaddleOCR processes documents/images, so if those inputs contain regulated data, the operator must ensure the processing environment matches policy; python-cheatsheet itself adds no extra compliance burden.
conditions: IF regulated documents are sent to agent_a, then the operator must verify the hosting and retention policy.
IF future deployment places either agent under a different jurisdiction or retention regime, then compliance must be rechecked.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to agent_a.
Document retention for any OCR inputs and outputs.
Keep both agents in the same approved compliance boundary.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated document classes.
